headline: Fuel-price gains lift revenue, but EPS falls sharply
summary_short: Arko reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2,346.5M, up 17.4% y/y, while basic EPS fell 75.0% y/y to $0.04.
summary_long: Revenue rose 17.4% y/y to $2,346.5M as higher retail, wholesale, and GPMP fuel prices offset lower same-store gallons and volume lost to retail-to-dealer conversions. Operating income fell 46.4% y/y to $30.4M as reduced retail fuel and merchandise contribution from converted/closed stores outweighed wholesale and GPMP margin gains. Net income attributable to Arko fell 69.6% y/y to $6.1M and basic EPS dropped 75.0% to $0.04, largely because net income now carries a minority-interest deduction for APC following its February 2026 IPO. Cash fell 16.4% y/y to $245.6M after roughly $206.7M of IPO proceeds repaid revolver debt; total liquidity including credit availability was about $1.0 billion. The board maintained its $0.03/share quarterly dividend.
confidence_notes: Net income y/y comparability is affected by ARKO Petroleum Corp. (APC) minority interest following its Feb 13, 2026 IPO — a structural, not operational, driver of the EPS decline.

drivers.explanation: Fuel revenue rose on higher average retail and wholesale prices, partly offset by lower same-store gallons and volume lost to stores converted to dealer locations.
Retail fuel and merchandise contribution fell from stores closed or converted to dealer locations, outweighing wholesale and GPMP fixed-margin gains.
Net income attributable to Arko dropped mainly because results now include a minority-interest deduction for APC following its February 2026 IPO.
Cash fell after Arko used about $206.7 million of APC IPO proceeds to repay Capital One Line of Credit borrowings.
Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA both grew on fuel-price gains and segment mix, but per-share profit fell on conversion volume loss and the new APC minority interest.
